question: Which of the following types of asexual reproduction is shown by the bread mould Rhizopus?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Spore formation.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **bread mould Rhizopus** shows **spore formation **as a type of asexual reproduction.
 
• Spore formation involves the production of **haploid spores **by the parent organism, which can grow into new individuals.
 
• In Rhizopus, the spores are produced in specialized structures called **sporangia,** which are found on the tips of hyphae.
 
• Spore formation allows for** rapid reproduction and dispersal of offspring**, as the spores can be carried away by wind or other means.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Budding **is a type of **asexual reproduction **where a small outgrowth or bud develops on the parent organism and eventually separates to form a new individual. 

 
 
• Budding is shown by **yeast, hydra**, and some other organisms.
 
 
 
• **Regeneration** involves the **regrowth of lost body parts.** 
 
 
• Regeneration is shown by **planarians, starfish**, and some other organisms.
 
 
 
• **Fission i**nvolves the **splitting of the parent organism** into two or more parts, each of which can grow into a new individual.
 
 
• Fission is shown by **bacteria** and some other** unicellular **organisms.
